text:
All three tools are already in your tree — `apps/system/nxrecorder`, `nxplayer`, and **`nxlooper`**.

## The mechanism

The codec driver registers character devices — a capture node and a playback node. From there it's just file I/O:

```
mic → ES8311 ADC → I2S → DMA → /dev/audio/pcm0c   (read)
/dev/audio/pcm0p → DMA → I2S → ES8311 DAC → amp → speaker   (write)
```

`nxrecorder` reads the capture node into a `.wav` on the SD card. `nxplayer` writes a `.wav` back out. **`nxlooper` does both at once** — it reads capture and writes playback in a loop, so you talk and hear yourself with a few ms of delay. That's the fastest possible test: no file, no card, no transfer. Run it, speak, and you either hear yourself or you don't.

```
nsh> nxlooper
nxlooper> loopback
```

## How playback tells you anything

It's not that playback is interesting. It's that **your ear is a fast, high-resolution instrument** and every fault in this chain has a distinct sound:

| What you hear | What's broken |
|---|---|
| Your voice, clean | Whole chain works. Done. |
| Nothing at all | Codec never initialized — I²C address wrong, or MCLK off |
| Silence, but no errors | Mic gain at default zero (`ES8311_ADC_REG16`) |
| Chipmunk / slow-motion | Sample-rate mismatch between codec and I²S |
| White noise / roar | Wrong bit depth, or byte order swapped |
| Voice + loud hiss | Gain too high, or analog supply noise |
| Clean but choppy | DMA buffers too small, or losing to LVGL/camera |
| Playback works, capture dead | Codec in DAC-only mode — `audio_mode` not set to `ES_MODULE_ADC` |

Every one of those returns **success** from every API call. There is no error code to read. Seven distinct faults, separated in one second of listening.

That's the whole argument: this is the only instrument you have that can see the analog and timing layers at all. A debugger can't tell you the mic gain is zero — the buffers are full of valid, well-formed, correctly-timed samples that happen to all be near zero.

## What it does *not* test

Playback proves the plumbing, not the intelligence. It says nothing about whether a model can tell "King" from "breakfast." That's the separate, larger problem — and it's the one you *want* to be working on with everything below it already proven.

So the order is: `nxlooper` proves the pipe → `nxrecorder` fills a dataset from the real mic in the real enclosure → train a keyword model on that data → wire the recognized word into the schedule UI.

text:
Yes — and you've already proven the pattern. Look at what `backend_tflm.cc` does today:

```cpp
static tflite::MicroMutableOpResolver<16> resolver;      // model 1
static tflite::MicroInterpreter interp(g_model, resolver, g_arena, kArenaSize);

static tflite::MicroMutableOpResolver<10> bcs_res;       // model 2
... MicroInterpreter(..., g_bcs_arena, kBcsArena);
```

Two independent interpreters, each with **its own resolver and its own arena** — the comment at line 204 even says so explicitly. A third is that same recipe a third time. You're not discovering a new architecture, you're repeating one that already runs on your hardware.

## The cheap parts

**Flash:** a KWS model is ~20–40 KB. Against your 1.4 MB MobileNetV3, it's a rounding error. And it's small enough for the **rodata embed** path your TFLM notes mark as a green path — no flash-load-to-PSRAM thread, no `.bss`-stack cache dance. It's *simpler* than either existing model.

**RAM:** arena ~20–30 KB, next to your 768 KB. On 8 MB PSRAM, noise.

**Ops:** declare a third resolver, e.g. `MicroMutableOpResolver<8>`. No interaction with the other two. Just don't undercount the template parameter — that's a silent failure at `AllocateTensors`.

## The expensive part, and it's not model count

`CONFIG_SMP` isn't in your defconfig, so **you're single-core.** Everything time-shares one CPU.

That matters because the third model has a fundamentally different duty cycle from the first two:

| | Trigger | Duration | Duty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pet recognition | camera capture | 1310 ms | on demand |
| BCS | camera capture | on demand | on demand |
| **Keyword spotting** | **never stops** | ~10–20 ms | **continuous** |

Models 1 and 2 are events. A cat walks up, you burn 1310 ms, you're done. KWS is a *treadmill* — a rolling window, re-inferring every few tens of ms, forever, on the same core already running LVGL, the camera pipeline, and audio DMA.

The collision is concrete: **during a 1310 ms recognition, KWS either starves and misses the wake word, or preempts and makes recognition slower.** On one core you don't get both.

## The fix, which you already have

Don't run the model continuously. Gate it behind **VAD** — voice activity detection. `apps/audioutils/speexdsp` is already in your tree with VAD, noise suppression and AGC. VAD is cheap DSP on raw samples: it answers "is anyone talking?" for a fraction of the cost of an inference.

```
audio DMA → VAD (cheap, always on) → [speech?] → MFCC → KWS model (expensive, rare)
```

In a quiet kitchen the model runs approximately never. That turns a permanent load into an occasional one and the contention mostly evaporates.

The remaining real risk is **audio buffer underrun during that 1310 ms inference** — DMA keeps filling in hardware, but if no thread drains it in time you drop samples and lose the word. That's a buffer-sizing question, and it's the thing I'd actually watch. Not the third model.

## Short version

Three models is fine; that's the settled part. What's new isn't a model, it's a **continuously-running workload on a single-core system that currently only does bursty work.** Budget your worry there.
cant the third model live in sdcard?

No — and the reason is the thing we found today.

## The microSD slot *is* the stepper

```
J8.14  IO9   SD_MISO   → STEP_IN1
J8.12  IO10  SD_MOSI   → STEP_IN2
J8.10  IO11  SD_SCLK   → STEP_IN3
```

Those are the same three pins. The card slot and the motor are wired to the same GPIOs, and the motor got there first. There is no microSD on this build — not for models, not for anything.

Your hardware notes still list "microSD → persistent feed history" as a feature this board unlocks. That's dead. Fortunately you already solved it elsewhere: enrolled pets, schedules, and embeddings live at flash `0x800000`, photos at `0x810000`. Nothing was lost — but the SD card should come off the BOM.

## Even with free pins, it wouldn't work

TFLM doesn't stream. `tflite::GetModel(ptr)` takes a pointer to a flatbuffer that must stay valid and randomly addressable for the interpreter's entire life — **weights are read directly out of the flatbuffer during every inference**, not copied into the arena. That's the whole design of the format.

So "model on SD" can only ever mean: read the entire file into RAM at boot, then point TFLM at the RAM copy. You'd save zero RAM, and you'd have swapped a fast, always-present flash read for a slower one that fails if the card is missing or corrupt. It's strictly worse than what you do today for the big models.

## And you aren't short on space anyway

I think the worry behind the question is that a third model is a burden. It isn't — at least not this way:

- `velapaw.tflite` at `0x600000`, `bcs.tflite` at `0x760000`, persistence at `0x800000`. That's a **640 KB gap** sitting unused after the BCS model.
- A KWS model is 20–40 KB.

Better still: **skip flash entirely and embed it in rodata**, the small-model path your own TFLM notes mark as green. No offset, no `esptool` line, no flash-load thread, no cache-suspend `.bss` stack dance. It rides inside `nuttx.bin` as a `const uint8_t[]` and TFLM points straight at it. That's the simplest of the three models to load, by a wide margin.

Storage was never the constraint. **CPU time on a single core is** — and an SD card doesn't help with that at all.

## One correction

Two messages ago I said `nxrecorder` would write `.wav` files "on the SD card." That's wrong, for the reason above. For dataset collection you'll want to stream PCM over the USB-CDC console and capture it on the host, or buffer to RAM and dump. `nxlooper` needs no storage at all, so the first smoke test is unaffected.
so what are the odds on the cpu?

Let me actually compute it instead of hand-waving, and calibrate off *your* measured number rather than published benchmarks.

## First, a correction

I said KWS inference would be "10–20 ms." That was borrowed from generic ESP32-S3 benchmarks, not from your hardware. Calibrating against your own data point instead:

Your MobileNetV3 takes **1310 ms** with ESP-NN full kernels. A standard DS-CNN-S keyword model is roughly 2.7 M MACs against that model's ~60–100 M. Scaling by your measured throughput:

**KWS inference ≈ 30–60 ms**, not 10–20. That's a 3× miss and it changes the arithmetic.

MFCC is genuinely cheap, though — a 512-point FFT plus a 40-bin filterbank per frame, ~100 µs, 50 frames/sec ≈ **0.5% CPU**. The frontend is not your problem.

## The arithmetic

| Design | Load on the one core |
|---|---|
| Ungated, 100 ms stride | 40 ms / 100 ms = **~40%, permanent** |
| Ungated, 200 ms stride | ~20%, and you start missing words between windows |
| **VAD-gated** | **~2% idle**, spiking to ~40% only while someone speaks |

Ungated is not viable. A permanent 40% tax on a single core that also drives LVGL and a 1310 ms inference will show up as visible UI lag. VAD gating is not an optimization here — it's the design. In a quiet kitchen the model runs approximately never, and speexdsp is already in your tree.

## My odds

Estimates, stated as such:

- **A third TFLM model coexists with the other two — ~90%.** Your code already runs two independent interpreters with separate arenas and resolvers. This is the proven part.
- **KWS runs without wrecking the UI, given VAD gating — ~75%.** Contingent on the design, not on luck.
- **Ungated continuous KWS performs acceptably — ~25%.** Don't build it that way.
- **CPU is the thing that kills voice control — ~15%.**

That last number is the one you asked for, and it's low. Here's the thing worth internalizing: **CPU is not your main risk.** Training a keyword model that reliably separates "King" from "breakfast" from background kitchen noise, with a dataset you have to collect yourself, is a much bigger bet than 40 ms of inference. I'd put *that* at closer to 50% inside your remaining schedule.

## The failure mode I'd actually watch

Not throughput — **audio buffer underrun during that 1310 ms inference.**

DMA keeps filling in hardware, but on a single core, if your audio-drain thread doesn't get scheduled while the recognition worker is grinding, buffers overflow and samples vanish. You don't get an error. You just miss the wake word every time a pet happens to be at the bowl — the exact moment you most want it to work.

Two mitigations, both cheap, both must be designed in rather than discovered:

1. **Audio drain thread priority above the inference worker.** Your recognition runs on a detached worker; if it sits at equal or higher priority and doesn't block, it starves audio. One-line fix, invisible failure if you miss it.
2. **Size DMA buffers for ≥2 s.** 16 kHz × 16-bit mono = 32 KB/s, so 64 KB of PSRAM covers the whole worst-case inference. Trivial against your 8 MB.

There is an escape hatch — the S3 has a second core and NuttX supports SMP — but given what `CONFIG_RTC` did to your console, I would not turn on SMP on a working build weeks before a deadline. Keep it as a last resort.

# VelaPaw — Voice Control Plan (ES8311 onboard mic)

Status: **not started.** Written 2026-08-02, after the schematic netlist review that
proved the onboard mic is reachable without touching the stepper.

## Why this is possible at all

The ES8311 codec's I²S bus is **GPIO 12/13/14/15/16**, and those nets are private —
each has exactly two nodes, the ESP32 and the codec. They are not on header J8, so
nothing external can reach them *or* conflict with them. The stepper lives on
9/10/11/43 (header pins 14/12/10/27). Audio and the feeder cannot collide
electrically. See `SESSION_STATE.md` for the full J8 map.

The mic is analog-differential into `MIC1P`/`MIC1N`; the bundled 6 Ω 1 W speaker runs
through an NS4150B amp whose enable is `PA_CTRL` = expander **EXIO7**. Codec control
shares the existing IO7/IO8 I²C bus. **No new parts, no new wiring.**

---

## PHASE 0 — Rollback net (MUST complete before Phase 1)

Three legs. All three, or don't start.

### Leg 1 — Source baseline (Windows, D:)

The repo currently has **one commit** (the scaffold) and every piece of real work is
untracked. There is no source rollback today. Fix that first:

```bash
cd D:/openVela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge
git add -A -- . ':!logs'          # everything EXCEPT logs/ (uploaded separately)
git commit -s -m "baseline: VelaPaw working state before audio/voice work"
git tag pre-audio
```

`logs/` is deliberately excluded — those are AI-coding session logs, pushed on their
own cadence by the operator.

Rollback: `git checkout pre-audio -- board/ app/ docs/`

### Leg 2 — Golden binary (the one that actually saves you)

Git restores *source*. It does not give you a working firmware — the build lives in
the Linux VM and takes a full rebuild to reproduce. Copy the currently-flashed
artifacts out of the VM to a path that is never touched:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio
cp nuttx/nuttx.bin                                   ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
cp nuttx/.config                                     ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/defconfig.golden
cp <repo>/app/velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite     ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
cp <repo>/app/velapaw/infer/model/bcs.tflite         ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
cp <BOARD>/src/esp32s3_st7789.c                      ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
```

⚠️ That last file is the **authoritative** stepper source. The repo copy has never
been validated against it (see the drive-table delta noted in `SESSION_STATE.md`).
Diff them while you are in there.

Rollback, ~60 seconds, no rebuild:

```bash
esptool --chip esp32s3 --port <PORT> write-flash \
  0x0      ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/nuttx.bin \
  0x600000 ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/velapaw.tflite \
  0x760000 ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/bcs.tflite
```

### Leg 3 — Work on a branch

```bash
git switch -c audio
```

`main` keeps pointing at the working state. Same shape as the `spi-lcd-lab` pattern
that worked last time: golden backup + isolated workspace.

---

## PHASE 1 — Prove the pipe (go/no-go gate)

**Goal:** speak, hear yourself. Nothing else. No model, no recognition.

### defconfig delta

Verified against `nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Kconfig`:

```
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_ROLE_MASTER=y      # required for MCLK
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_RX=y               # default y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_TX=y               # default y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLK=y             # default n — MUST enable, codec is dead without it
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLKPIN=12
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_BCLKPIN=13         # default 4  ← would collide with LCD CS
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14          # default 19 — ASDOUT, codec → ESP (capture)
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_WSPIN=15           # default 5  ← would collide with LCD SCLK
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DOUTPIN=16         # default 18 — DSDIN, ESP → codec (playback)
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_SAMPLE_RATE=16000  # default 44100; voice only needs 16k

CONFIG_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311=y
CONFIG_AUDIO_FORMAT_PCM=y
CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXLOOPER=y
```

🔴 **The four pin defaults are the dangerous part.** `BCLKPIN` defaults to 4 (LCD chip
select) and `WSPIN` to 5 (LCD SCLK). Enabling I²S without overriding them will break
the display. Set all five pins explicitly in the same edit that enables I²S.

### Board glue

`nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/src/esp32s3_es8311.c` already exists upstream,
gated on `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S && CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311`. Call
`esp32s3_es8311_initialize()` from board init. No driver to write.

### Test

```
nsh> nxlooper
nxlooper> loopback
```

### Diagnosis table

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Your voice, clean | Pipe works. Gate passed. |
| Console dies / no boot | Config landmine — same class as `CONFIG_RTC`. Revert, bisect. |
| Display breaks | I²S pins left at defaults (4/5). Fix `BCLKPIN`/`WSPIN`. |
| Nothing at all | Codec never initialised — I²C address, or MCLK not enabled |
| Silence, no errors | Mic gain at 0 — `ES8311_ADC_REG16` |
| Chipmunk / slow-motion | Sample-rate mismatch codec vs I²S |
| White noise / roar | Wrong bit depth or byte order |
| Choppy | DMA buffers too small |
| Playback OK, capture dead | Codec in DAC-only mode — `audio_mode` not `ES_MODULE_ADC` |

**None of these throw an error.** Your ear is the instrument.

### Order of operations (do not batch)

1. Enable I²S + pins only. Boot. **Confirm console AND display still work.**
2. Add codec + audio. Boot. Confirm console still works.
3. Add nxlooper. Test.

Batching all three is how you end up bisecting three interacting failures at once.

### ABORT CRITERIA

If Phase 1 is not passing after **~2 working sessions**, stop and reflash the golden
binary. Voice control is a stretch feature; the enclosure assembly and the open JLC
reorders are committed deliverables and outrank it.

---

## PHASE 2 — Dataset

`nxrecorder` writes to a filesystem. **There is no microSD** — the slot's pins are the
stepper (IO9/10/11). Stream PCM over the USB-CDC console and capture on the host, or
buffer to RAM and dump.

Record through **this mic, in the printed enclosure, in the real room**, with the
stepper running for part of it. A model trained on clean laptop audio will
underperform here — mic response, housing resonance, and motor noise all matter.

Vocabulary — keep it small, this is a dialog tree, not a sentence parser:

```
"Hi VelaPaw"  →  "schedule"  →  <pet name>  →  <meal>  →  <hour>
```

Target ~10–15 words plus silence/unknown.

## PHASE 3 — Train (host side)

`host/` already has TensorFlow and a working export pipeline from the pet and BCS
models. Add a KWS training script alongside them. Target: DS-CNN-S class, int8
quantised, **20–40 KB**.

## PHASE 4 — On device

Third TFLM interpreter. The pattern is already proven in `app/velapaw/infer/backend_tflm.cc`,
which runs two independent interpreters with separate arenas and resolvers — do it a
third time with its own `MicroMutableOpResolver<8>` and a ~30 KB arena.

**Embed the model in rodata**, do not flash-load it. At this size it rides inside
`nuttx.bin` as a `const uint8_t[]` — no flash offset, no `esptool` line, no
cache-suspend `.bss`-stack thread. Simplest of the three models by far.

### The two real risks (neither is model count)

1. **Continuous duty cycle on a single core.** `CONFIG_SMP` is off. Ungated KWS at a
   100 ms stride costs ~40 % of the core, permanently, against LVGL + camera + a
   1310 ms recognition. **Gate it behind VAD** — `apps/audioutils/speexdsp` is already
   in the tree. Cheap DSP decides "is anyone talking"; the expensive model only runs
   when the answer is yes. Quiet kitchen → model runs ~never.

2. **Audio underrun during the 1310 ms inference.** DMA keeps filling; if the drain
   thread isn't scheduled, samples vanish silently and the wake word is missed at
   exactly the moment a pet is at the bowl. Two mitigations, both must be designed in:
   - audio drain thread priority **above** the recognition worker
   - DMA buffers sized for ≥2 s (16 kHz × 16-bit mono = 32 KB/s → 64 KB PSRAM)

Do not enable `CONFIG_SMP` to solve this. Recall what `CONFIG_RTC` did to the console.

## PHASE 5 — Wire to the UI

Recognized word → the existing schedule path (`velapaw_main.c`, `def_meals[]`) and the
Model-B recognition-gated meal times. Screen shows "🎤 Listening…" and echoes the
recognized word — the 3.5" display is the audio feedback channel, which is arguably
better than a beep and works even if the speaker path lags.

---

## Scope honesty

Free-form speech — *"velapaw schedule the first feeding time for pet king at 8"* as one
spoken sentence — **will not work on-device.** No ASR engine exists in the openVela
tree and there is no room for one. On-device gets you a guided dialog tree. The literal
sentence requires cloud NLU via `external/bailian_sdk` (`libqwen_sdk.a`,
`libc_mmi_cmd_voice_translate.a` are vendored in-tree).

Confidence: Phase 1 passing is likely. A *usable* keyword model inside the remaining
schedule is roughly a coin flip — the bet is the dataset and training, not the CPU.

# Snapshot — 2026-08-02, pre-audio

Point-in-time copy of `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge` taken **before any
audio / voice-control work began**. 215 files, 20.9 MB.

This is a plain file copy, not a git commit. To restore, copy directories back over

## What's here

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Continuation of the **VelaPaw** contest project (team **contest2026_043_CircuitForge**; GitHub login **KingMbewe**; project at **D:\openVela**, NOT C:). This window covered a chain of requests that evolved from a hardware feasibility question into a full baseline-verification exercise:

   (a) *"will a breadboard help"* — whether a breadboard solves the microphone-wiring problem.

   (b) *"look at this"* + the full **ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5 schematic PDF** — verify the pin availability question against the actual netlist.

   (c) *"yes"* — approval to (i) fix the stepper pin defines in `board/esp32s3_st7789.c` and (ii) update `velapaw-hardware.md`.

   (d) *"so it will work?"* / *"what does codec do"* / *"so why record an audio instead of free speech"* / *"so how will it work by playing the audio?"* — a sequence of feasibility and explanation questions about the voice-control path.

   (e) *"but i already have two models will a third model work?"* and *"cant the third model live in sdcard?"* — capacity questions about adding a third TFLM model.

   (f) **"okay so write a plan so that we can start but before that make sure that we can be able to roll back to the version without the audio thing"** — write the voice-control plan, but establish rollback capability FIRST.

   (g) **"no dont do that I think for now just have a snapshot of how things are...so that we can be able to build the working version again"** — **explicit rejection of the git commit approach**; the user wants a plain file snapshot instead.

   (h) *"Give me the commands to do in vm"* — VM-side commands for the golden binary backup, followed by several rounds of executing them and pasting output.

   **STANDING CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST PERSIST (verbatim intent):**
   - **"log no push"**: AI-coding logs go into `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\logs\KingMbewe\` — **write files ONLY, NEVER git commit/push**.
   - **The user declined the git baseline commit.** Do not run `git add`/`git commit`/`git tag` on the contest repo unless newly asked. Use file snapshots instead.
   - **Never enable CONFIG_RTC** (kills the USB-CDC console; PCF85063 RTC driven directly over I²C instead).
   - Raw `spi_flash` write at offset **0x818000 WEDGES the SoC**.
   - **`-fno-threadsafe-statics` is mandatory** on C++ flags (else TFLM init deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire`).
   - Console is on **USB-Serial/JTAG (CDCACM)**, not UART0.
   - Stepper **IN4 must be GPIO43 (not GPIO44** — U0RXD is clamped and cannot drive an output).
   - A **reversed FFC cable is FATAL on first power-on** — verify orientation with a meter before power.
   - **Do NOT enable `CONFIG_SMP`** on a working build weeks before the deadline (recall what CONFIG_RTC did to the console).
   - **RETRACTED this session:** my earlier rule "never enable `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` / `esp32s3_es8311.c`" was based on a false premise (that the codec bus collided with the stepper). It does not. Enabling that glue is now the *recommended* path.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

   - **Schematic netlist parsing**: the PDF's flattened netlist uses `PI<ref><pin>` node identifiers followed by `NL<netname>` labels. A net with only one `PI` node is dangling/unbonded.
   - **ES8311 codec**: mono coder/decoder (analog↔digital), NOT compression. Capture: mic → MIC1P/MIC1N → preamp (`ES8311_ADC_REG16` gain) → ADC → I2S_ASDOUT. Playback: I2S_DSDIN → DAC → OUTP/OUTN → NS4150B amp → speaker. Two buses: I²S = data, I²C = control.
   - **NuttX audio stack**: `nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.c` supports `AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT`; `esp32s3_i2s.c` has `i2s_receive()`; `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_RX` defaults `y`. Board glue `nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/src/esp32s3_es8311.c` exists upstream, gated on `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S && CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311`, exposing `esp32s3_es8311_initialize()`.
   - **NuttX audio apps present in tree**: `apps/system/` contains `nxcamera`, `nxcodec`, `nxdiag`, `nxlooper`, `nxplayer`, `nxrecorder`. **`nxlooper` (mic→speaker realtime loopback) is the fastest smoke test.**
   - **TFLM multi-model pattern**: each model needs its own `MicroMutableOpResolver<N>`, its own arena, its own `MicroInterpreter`. `GetModel(ptr)` requires a persistent, randomly-addressable flatbuffer — **weights are read directly from it during inference, never copied into the arena**, so a model cannot be streamed from storage.
   - **KWS cost calibration**: extrapolating from their measured 1310 ms MobileNetV3, a DS-CNN-S class keyword model is **~30–60 ms** (I initially and wrongly said 10–20 ms). MFCC frontend ≈ 0.5% CPU. Ungated at 100 ms stride = ~40% of one core permanently.
   - **VAD gating** via `apps/audioutils/speexdsp` is the design, not an optimization.
   - **`CONFIG_MATH_KISSFFT=y` is already enabled** — an FFT library is in the build, useful for an MFCC frontend.
   - **No ASR engine exists in openVela.** Free-form sentence recognition is impossible on-device; cloud path is `external/bailian_sdk` (`libqwen_sdk.a`, `libc_mmi_cmd_voice_translate.a`).

# Snapshot — 2026-08-02, pre-audio

Point-in-time copy of `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge` taken **before any
audio / voice-control work began**. 215 files, ~21 MB.

This is a plain file copy, not a git commit. To restore, copy directories back over
the working tree.

**Refreshed 2026-08-02 21:02**, after the sources were reconciled against the golden
copy in the VM. The earlier revision of this file carried a "THIS IS NOT THE FIRMWARE
ON THE BOARD" warning — that warning is resolved. See *Provenance* below.

## What's here

| | |
|---|---|
| `board/` | `esp32s3_st7789.c`, `esp32s3_appinit.c`, `configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig` |
| `app/velapaw/` | full app incl. the **untracked `Makefile`** and both `.tflite` models |
| `hardware/` | SCAD sources + STLs |
| `docs/` | engineering notes, `SESSION_STATE.md`, `AUDIO_PLAN.md` |
| `host/` | training pipeline scripts |
| `schema/`, `.github/`, README/USAGE/JUDGE_GUIDE | |

**Excluded:** `.git/`, `host/.venv/`, `host/data/` (755 MB dataset tarball),
`host/export*/`, `__pycache__/`, `logs/`, build artifacts. All regenerable or
separately managed. `logs/` was left out on purpose — session logs are a separate
deliverable with their own upload cadence.

## Provenance — how this relates to the flashed firmware

The firmware on the board is `nuttx.bin`, 816,308 B, built **2026-07-24 10:51:26** in
the Linux VM. It is preserved, md5summed and write-protected, at
`~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/` in the VM, along with the VM's `.config` and the two
board source files.

Both board files in this snapshot were reconciled against that golden copy on
2026-08-02:

- `board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig` — **byte-identical** to the VM (2,894 B).
  The repo had been missing `CONFIG_VELAPAW_FONT_CJK=y`, which was exactly the 26-byte
  difference.
- `board/esp32s3_st7789.c` — **behaviourally identical, not byte-identical.** Every
  constant, the drive table, the bit order, and the control flow match the VM. This
  copy is ~1.4 KB larger because it carries additional comments (the J8 pin map, the
  IO12–16 warning, the full-step rationale) that the VM copy does not.

The stepper block specifically now matches: pins `9/10/11/43`, `k_fullstep[4] =
{0x3, 0x6, 0xC, 0x9}` with **bit0 = IN1**, `STEP_PER_REV 2048`, `STEP_DELAY_US 3000`,
`GRAMS_PER_POCKET 5`, `feeder_pins_output()` re-called at the top of every dispense.
Before reconciliation this snapshot held a half-step table with the **opposite bit
order**, which would have driven the rotor backwards.

## Rebuild from this snapshot

```bash
BOARD=nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit
cp board/esp32s3_st7789.c   $BOARD/src/
cp board/esp32s3_appinit.c  $BOARD/src/
cp board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig
./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8
```

Flash:

```bash
esptool --chip esp32s3 --port <PORT> write-flash \
  0x0      nuttx/nuttx.bin \
  0x600000 app/velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite \
  0x760000 app/velapaw/infer/model/bcs.tflite
```

⚠️ Never raw-write `spi_flash` at `0x818000` — it wedges the SoC.

**Note:** the rebuild is not bit-reproducible against the golden `nuttx.bin` — the
extra comments alone change nothing, but toolchain and build-tree state in the VM are
not captured here. This snapshot is *source*. For a guaranteed-working board, reflash
the golden binary; for a guaranteed-working *build*, rebuild from this.

## Faster path: reflash the golden binary

~60 seconds, no rebuild, no toolchain:

```bash
esptool --chip esp32s3 --port <PORT> write-flash \
  0x0      ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/nuttx.bin \
  0x600000 <repo>/app/velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite \
  0x760000 <repo>/app/velapaw/infer/model/bcs.tflite
```

⚠️ **One gap left in the golden set:** the two `.tflite` models are not in
`~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/` — the `cp` failed silently because the contest repo is
not checked out at that path in the VM. The models are safe here in this snapshot and
in the repo, but the golden directory is not self-contained yet. To close it:

```bash
chmod u+w ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio
cp <repo>/app/velapaw/infer/model/{velapaw,bcs}.tflite ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
cd ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio && md5sum * > MANIFEST.md5 && chmod -R a-w .
```

## Standing rule

**The VM board tree is authoritative for `board/`.** Anything edited there gets copied
back to `D:` in the same session. That is how the half-step/full-step drift happened.

## What the drift actually was

**`defconfig` — 26 bytes, one line:** the repo was missing `CONFIG_VELAPAW_FONT_CJK=y`. Everything else was byte-identical. **`esp32s3_st7789.c` — the dangerous one.** The repo had a half-step table with the **opposite bit order**:

| | repo (was) | VM (running) |
|---|---|---|
| table | `k_halfstep[8] = {0x8,0xC,0x4,0x6,0x2,0x3,0x1,0x9}` | `k_fullstep[4] = {0x3,0x6,0xC,0x9}` |

| rev / delay / pocket | 4096 / 1500 µs / 4 g | 2048 / 3000 µs / 5 g |
| phase mask | `& 7` | `& 3` |

The bit order is reversed, so a rebuild from Windows would have driven the rotor **backwards** — food would never have reached the outlet, and it would have looked like a mechanical fault, not a source one. Two separate problems. `<repo>` was a placeholder I left unfilled — my fault, and we don't actually know the models exist in the VM at all. And `chmod u+w` on the *directory* doesn't unlock the read-only `MANIFEST.md5` file inside it.

First find out whether the models are even in the VM:

```bash
find ~ -name '*.tflite' -not -path '*/velapaw-golden/*' 2>/dev/null | xargs -r ls -l
```

**If that prints paths**, fix the permissions properly (`-R`) and use the real path:

```bash
chmod -R u+w ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio
cp /path/to/velapaw.tflite /path/to/bcs.tflite ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/
cd ~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio && md5sum * > MANIFEST.md5 && chmod -R a-w .
ls -l
```

**If it prints nothing**, the models aren't in the VM — they only exist on Windows at `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw\infer\model\`. That's consistent with what we found earlier: the contest repo isn't checked out in the VM; the app lives at `/home/king/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw` and the models get pushed in at flash time from the Windows side.

In that case pull them over with the HTTP loop you already use. On Windows:

```powershell
cd D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw\infer\model
py -m http.server 9100
```

wget http://192.168.160.1:9100/bcs.tflite

input.new_string:
### Order of operations (do not batch)

**Correction, 2026-08-02:** an earlier version of this plan said step 1 was "I²S and
pins only". **That will not link.** `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y` unconditionally compiles
`boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/src/esp32s3_board_i2s.c`, and the devkit bringup
unconditionally calls its `board_i2sdev_initialize()`, which calls
`audio_i2s_initialize()`, `audio_register()` and `pcm_decode_initialize()`. Without the
audio framework those are undefined symbols. I²S and the audio core are one step,
whether you want them to be or not.

1. **I²S + pins + audio core**, no codec. Boot. **Confirm console AND display still
   work.** This is the step that can break the LCD (pin defaults) and the console.
2. **Add `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` + the init call.** Boot. Confirm console survives.
   This is the step that can hang on I²C.
3. **`nxlooper` → `loopback`.** Test with your ears.

The split that matters is *codec vs no codec* — the codec driver probes I²C at init and
is the part that can hang. Step 1 only brings up a DMA peripheral on five pins that go
nowhere else.

### What step 1 actually needs

```
CONFIG_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_AUDIO_I2S=y            # audio_i2s_initialize()
CONFIG_DRIVERS_AUDIO=y        # note: "menuconfig DRIVERS_AUDIO", drivers/audio/Kconfig
CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXLOOPER=y      # also short-circuits the pcm_decode path in board_i2s.c
```

`CONFIG_AUDIO_FORMAT_PCM` defaults to `y` under `AUDIO`, so it comes free and
`savedefconfig` will strip it. Same for `I2S0_RX`/`I2S0_TX` (default y),
`I2S0_ROLE_MASTER` and `I2S0_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT` (both choice defaults). Don't be
surprised when they're absent from the file.

`ESP32S3_I2S0` also `select`s `ESP32S3_DMA`, `ESP32S3_GPIO_IRQ` and **`SCHED_HPWORK`** —
a new kernel worker thread with its own stack, on a board where internal RAM is
`CONFIG_RAM_SIZE=114688`. Watch for heap pressure at boot.

text:
Yes — Phase 1 step 1 is ready, and verifying against the tree on `D:` first caught a real error in my own plan.

## What the verification changed

**Good news:** step 1 needs **zero code**. The devkit bringup already calls `board_i2sdev_initialize(ESP32S3_I2S0, tx, rx)` under a `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0` gate. Pure defconfig.

**The error:** my plan said step 1 was "I²S and pins only." That would not have linked. `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y` unconditionally compiles `esp32s3_board_i2s.c`, and the bringup unconditionally calls into it — which needs `audio_i2s_initialize()`, `audio_register()`, `pcm_decode_initialize()`. Without the audio framework those are undefined symbols. I²S and the audio core are one step whether or not I wanted them separated. The split that actually matters is **codec vs no codec**, since the ES8311 driver probes I²C at init and is the part that can hang.

Also confirmed the dangerous bit: `BCLKPIN` really does default to **4** (your LCD CS) and `WSPIN` to **5** (LCD SCLK).

## The change, already applied to the repo defconfig

```
CONFIG_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_AUDIO_I2S=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_BCLKPIN=13
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DOUTPIN=16
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLK=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLKPIN=12
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_SAMPLE_RATE=16000
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_WSPIN=15
CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXLOOPER=y
```

No `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` yet — that's step 2. `AUDIO_FORMAT_PCM`, `I2S0_RX/TX`, `ROLE_MASTER` and `16BIT` are all defaults, so they're deliberately absent.

## In the VM

```bash
cd ~/openvela
BOARD=nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit
cp $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig ~/defconfig.backup.preaudio-0802
cat >> $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig <<'EOF'
CONFIG_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_AUDIO_I2S=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_BCLKPIN=13
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DOUTPIN=16
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLK=y
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLKPIN=12
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_SAMPLE_RATE=16000
CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_WSPIN=15
CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXLOOPER=y
EOF
./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8
```

Append order doesn't matter — Kconfig sorts it, and `savedefconfig` will normalize later.

⚠️ **Expect the first build to fail.** Per your i18n notes, enabling a new Kconfig re-clones esp-hal, which reverts the `SP_UNLOCKED` spinlock patch → `invalid initializer`. Your `fix_hal` + retry wrapper handles it; the second build is clean. Don't debug that error, it's known.

## The gate — in this order

1. **Console.** `nsh>` over USB-CDC. If it's dead, this is `CONFIG_RTC` class — revert immediately.
2. **Display.** VelaPaw UI renders and touch works. If the LCD is broken, the pin overrides didn't take; check `.config` for `BCLKPIN=13`/`WSPIN=15`, not 4/5.
3. `ls /dev/audio` — expect a node from `board_i2sdev_initialize`.
4. Recognition still works. `SCHED_HPWORK` adds a kernel thread with its own stack on a board with 112 KB internal RAM, so watch for heap pressure at boot.

No sound yet — nothing is connected to the codec. Step 1 only proves the peripheral comes up without taking anything else down.

One caveat on scope: I verified symbol names, defaults, dependencies, and call sites against the source. I have not verified that the ESP32-S3 GDMA has a free channel alongside your SPI2+DMA display, or how `SCHED_HPWORK` interacts with the recognition worker. Those are runtime questions and are exactly what the four checks above are for.

Predicted failure, and it's the known one. The `Cloning Espressif HAL` line is the tell — changing the config re-cloned esp-hal and blew away your spinlock patch. **Everything else compiled**, including all the new I²S code.

I found the exact cause. In this NuttX, `spinlock_t` is a **struct**:

```c
} spinlock_t;
#  define SP_UNLOCKED {SPINLOCK_DEBUG_INIT 0}
```

so the HAL's `#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED 0` can't initialize it — you need the brace initializer.

## Patch and rebuild

```bash
cd ~/openvela
HAL=nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/chip/esp-hal-3rdparty/components/esp_hw_support/clk_ctrl_os.c
grep -n "LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED" $HAL
sed -i 's/^\(#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED[[:space:]]*\)0[[:space:]]*$/\1SP_UNLOCKED/' $HAL
grep -n "LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED" $HAL
./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8
```

The second `grep` should show `SP_UNLOCKED`. The rebuild won't re-clone the HAL — the config is unchanged now, which is why your second build always comes out clean.

## Make it stop costing you a cycle

This fires on *every* Kconfig change, so it'll hit again in step 2. Worth a script:

```bash
cat > ~/fix_hal.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# esp-hal re-clones on any Kconfig change, reverting the spinlock patch.
# spinlock_t is a struct here; SP_UNLOCKED is a brace initializer, 0 is not.
HAL=~/openvela/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/chip/esp-hal-3rdparty/components/esp_hw_support/clk_ctrl_os.c
[ -f "$HAL" ] || { echo "fix_hal: HAL not cloned yet"; exit 0; }
sed -i 's/^\(#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED[[:space:]]*\)0[[:space:]]*$/\1SP_UNLOCKED/' $HAL
grep -q "LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED[[:space:]]*SP_UNLOCKED" $HAL \
  && echo "fix_hal: patched" || echo "fix_hal: ALREADY OK or pattern changed"
EOF
chmod +x ~/fix_hal.sh
```

Then the standing recipe after any defconfig change is: `./build.sh ... ; ~/fix_hal.sh ; ./build.sh ...`.

## One real finding in the new code

The I²S driver you just enabled has a latent bug:

```
chip/esp32s3_i2s.c:2790:13: warning: implicit declaration of function 'nxmutex_lock'
chip/esp32s3_i2s.c:2820:7: warning: implicit declaration of function 'nxmutex_unlock'
```

`esp32s3_i2s.c` uses `nxmutex_lock`/`nxmutex_unlock` without including `<nuttx/mutex.h>`. It will link — `lib_sem_mutex_noinline.c` is in your build, so the real symbols exist — and on 32-bit the implicit `int`-returning declaration happens to pass the pointer correctly. So it works by luck, not by correctness.

Not blocking, don't fix it now. But if the link fails with `undefined reference to nxmutex_lock`, the fix is one line: add `#include <nuttx/mutex.h>` to `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

This window continues the **VelaPaw** contest project (team **contest2026_043_CircuitForge**, GitHub login **KingMbewe**, project at **D:\openVela**, NOT C:). It picks up mid-task from a prior compaction, where I had committed: *"Paste the output and I'll reconcile the repo to match what actually runs. Then Phase 1."*

The window covered four sequential intents:

**(a) Complete the repo↔VM reconciliation** using ground-truth data the user had pasted just before the previous compaction (VM stepper greps + full `defconfig.board`).

**(b) Close the golden-set gap** — copy the two `.tflite` models into `~/velapaw-golden/pre-audio/` so the rollback set is self-contained. The user ran my commands literally and hit two failures.

**(c) "okay so now we move to the audio work?"** — explicit approval to begin Phase 1 of `docs/AUDIO_PLAN.md` (onboard ES8311 mic/speaker voice control).

**(d) Execute Phase 1 step 1** — enable I²S + audio core in the defconfig, build in the VM, iterate on build failures.

### STANDING CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST PERSIST (verbatim intent)

- **"log no push"**: AI-coding logs go into `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\logs\KingMbewe\` — **write files ONLY, NEVER git commit/push**.
- **The user explicitly rejected the git baseline commit** ("no dont do that I think for now just have a snapshot of how things are"). Do NOT run `git add`/`git commit`/`git tag`/`git switch -c` on the contest repo unless newly asked. Rollback is plain file copies.
- **Never enable `CONFIG_RTC`** — it kills the USB-CDC console. PCF85063 RTC is driven directly over I²C.
- **Never raw-write `spi_flash` at offset `0x818000`** — it WEDGES the SoC.
- **`-fno-threadsafe-statics` is mandatory** on C++ flags, else TFLM init deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire`.
- Console is on **USB-Serial/JTAG (CDCACM)**, not UART0.
- Stepper **IN4 must be GPIO43, NOT GPIO44** (U0RXD is clamped and cannot drive an output).
- **Never move stepper coils to GPIO12/13/14/15/16** — private ESP32↔ES8311 I²S bus, not routed to any header.
- A **reversed FFC cable is FATAL on first power-on** — meter-verify orientation before power.
- **Do NOT enable `CONFIG_SMP`** on a working build weeks before the deadline.
- **The VM board tree is authoritative for `board/`** — anything edited there must be copied back to `D:` in the same session (this rule was established this session, after two silent drifts were found).
- **RETRACTED (prior session):** the rule "never enable `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311`" was based on a false premise and no longer applies.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **NuttX Kconfig `savedefconfig` semantics** — defaults and choice-defaults are stripped from `defconfig`; appending config fragments in any order works because `olddefconfig` normalizes.
- **`spinlock_t` is a struct in this NuttX**, with `SP_UNLOCKED` defined as a brace initializer (`{SPINLOCK_DEBUG_INIT 0}` / `{}` depending on config) in `nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock_type.h`. Scalar `0` is an invalid initializer.
- **esp-hal re-clone gotcha** — any Kconfig change re-clones `esp-hal-3rdparty`, reverting local patches. Recurs on every config change.
- **TFLM multi-model pattern** — each model needs its own `MicroMutableOpResolver<N>`, arena, and `MicroInterpreter`; weights are read directly from a persistent flatbuffer during inference, so a model cannot be streamed from storage.
- **TFLM `micro_speech` bundled assets** — pre-trained KWS model + an MFCC frontend expressed *as a tflite graph*, eliminating hand-written DSP and host/device feature divergence.
- **ES8311 codec** — analog differential mic into MIC1P/MIC1N; speaker via NS4150B amp whose enable `PA_CTRL` is expander **EXIO7** (not a GPIO, unlike korvo-2's `SPEAKER_ENABLE_GPIO`).
- **`board_i2sdev_initialize()`** — in `common/src/esp32s3_board_i2s.c`, compiled whenever `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S=y`, and unconditionally called by the devkit bringup. It requires the audio framework to link.
- **robocopy `/MIR` + `/XF`** — mirroring deletes files absent from source; `RESTORE.md` had to be excluded to survive refreshes.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\board\esp32s3_st7789.c` (MODIFIED — reconciled to VM)

The authoritative stepper source. The repo copy had drifted badly from what runs on the board.

Comment block changed from half-step to full-step:
```c
 * 28BYJ-48: 32 steps/motor-rev x ~63.68 gear, driven FULL-step (4-phase) =
 * ~2048 full steps per OUTPUT revolution. 6 pockets -> 2048/6 ~= 341 steps per
 * pocket. ...
 * Full-step, not half-step: two coils are energised at every phase, so torque
 * is roughly double and the rotor does not stall against the food column.
```

Constants + table + coil driver (now matching the VM exactly):
```c
#define STEP_IN1             9        /* J8 pin 14 (SD_MISO, slot unused) */
#define STEP_IN2             10       /* J8 pin 12 (SD_MOSI, slot unused) */
#define STEP_IN3             11       /* J8 pin 10 (SD_SCLK, slot unused) */
#define STEP_IN4             43       /* J8 pin 27 (U0TXD; NOT 44 -- clamped) */
#define ROTOR_POCKETS        6              /* vanes; must match the .scad */
#define STEP_PER_REV         2048           /* 28BYJ-48 FULL-step (64:1 gear) */
#define STEP_PER_POCKET      (STEP_PER_REV / ROTOR_POCKETS)   /* ~341 */
#define STEP_DELAY_US        3000
#define GRAMS_PER_POCKET     5              /* CALIBRATE: weigh one pocket */

static const uint8_t k_fullstep[4] =
  { 0x3, 0x6, 0xC, 0x9 };                   /* IN1+2, IN2+3, IN3+4, IN4+1 */

static void step_coils(uint8_t m)
{
  esp32s3_gpiowrite(STEP_IN1, (m & 0x1) != 0);
  esp32s3_gpiowrite(STEP_IN2, (m & 0x2) != 0);
  esp32s3_gpiowrite(STEP_IN3, (m & 0x4) != 0);
  esp32s3_gpiowrite(STEP_IN4, (m & 0x8) != 0);
}

static void feeder_pins_output(void)
{
  esp32s3_configgpio(STEP_IN1, OUTPUT);
  esp32s3_configgpio(STEP_IN2, OUTPUT);
  esp32s3_configgpio(STEP_IN3, OUTPUT);
  esp32s3_configgpio(STEP_IN4, OUTPUT);
}

void board_feeder_init(void)
{
  feeder_pins_output();
  step_coils(0);
  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[feeder] 28BYJ-48 stepper ready (ULN2003 on %d/%d/%d/%d)\n",
         STEP_IN1, STEP_IN2, STEP_IN3, STEP_IN4);
}

static void rotor_step(int n)
{
  static int phase = 0;
  int i;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      phase = (phase + 1) & 3;
      step_coils(k_fullstep[phase]);
      up_udelay(STEP_DELAY_US);
    }
  step_coils(0);
}

int board_feeder_dispense(int grams)
{
  int pockets;
  int steps;
  if (grams <= 0) return -1;

Voice control on the onboard ES8311 (`docs/AUDIO_PLAN.md`). Started 2026-08-02 from the
rollback net in [[velapaw-golden-baseline]].

## Step 1 ✅ DONE + FLASHED (2026-08-02) — I²S0 + audio core, no codec

13 defconfig lines: `AUDIO`, `AUDIO_I2S`, `DRIVERS_AUDIO`, `SYSTEM_NXLOOPER`,
`ESP32S3_I2S`, `ESP32S3_I2S0`, and I2S0 pins **BCLK=13 WS=15 DIN=14 DOUT=16 MCLK=12**,
16 kHz. **No code change needed** — the devkit bringup already calls
`board_i2sdev_initialize()` under `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0`.

⚠️ The Kconfig **defaults are BCLK=4 and WS=5, which are the LCD's CS and SCLK.** Always
set those pins explicitly and re-check them after `savedefconfig`.

On hardware: console/CDCACM re-enumerates, UI renders, touch responsive, Recognize
unchanged. `SCHED_HPWORK` (selected by `ESP32S3_I2S0`, prio 224 / 2 KB stack) caused no
visible heap or latency trouble.

**Judge linkage by the symbol table, not binary size.** `nuttx.bin` grew only **+1,392 B**
(816,308 → 817,700) which looked like the audio path had been garbage-collected;
`xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm nuttx | grep -w board_i2sdev_initialize` proved it was all there.
`--gc-sections` makes size a useless signal.

## The link failure that cost the most time

`undefined reference to nxmutex_lock/nxmutex_unlock` from `esp32s3_i2s.o`, preceded by an
`implicit declaration` warning. **Cause: the VM's `esp32s3_i2s.c` was missing
`#include <nuttx/mutex.h>`.** `CONFIG_LIBC_SEM_MUTEX_NOINLINE` is **off**, so those are
`static inline` bodies in the header — no exported symbol exists anywhere; an implicit
declaration turns them into extern calls that can never resolve. Adding the include is
the entire fix.

**Why:** I first "verified" the include was present by grepping `D:\openVela\nuttx` — the
*Windows* tree, which is not what the VM builds. The two `nuttx` checkouts are at
different revisions (Windows also carries a duplicate `#include <nuttx/semaphore.h>`).
**How to apply:** for anything about a build, grep the VM tree, never the Windows one.
Line numbers are the tell — the error said 2790, Windows said 2792.

## VM-only patches — a `repo sync` silently loses both

Neither is inside `contest2026_043_CircuitForge/`, so nothing tracks them:
1. `nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c` → add `#include <nuttx/mutex.h>`.
2. esp-hal `LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED` → `SP_UNLOCKED` (see [[velapaw-i18n]]; reverted by
   the re-clone that *any* Kconfig change triggers). **`~/fix_hal.sh` now genuinely exists
   in the VM** and is idempotent — it had been described in an earlier session but never
   actually written to disk. Run it before every build that changed config.

## BLOCKER: no working NSH console

Scripted `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort` access to COM4 gets **character echo but no `nsh>`
prompt and no command output** — on CR, LF and CRLF alike, and **identically on the
golden pre-audio firmware**, so it is not an audio regression. NuttX echoes in the driver
receive path with or without a reader, so echo proves nothing. Consequence: `/dev` could
not be listed, and **step 3 (`nxlooper` loopback ear test) cannot run at all** because
`nxlooper` is an NSH builtin. Solve shell access before step 3.

## Windows port map (from `Get-PnpDevice`)
- **COM3** `VID_303A&PID_1001` — Espressif USB-Serial/JTAG = **flash** port, appears only
  in ROM download mode (hold BOOT, tap RESET).
- **COM4** `VID_0525&PID_A4A7` — NuttX CDCACM gadget = **console** port, exists only while
  our firmware runs. Its presence after reset is a clean "did it boot?" test.
- `esptool` is not on PATH; use **`py -m esptool`** (v5.3.1, matches the VM).
- VM→Windows binary transfer: VM `python3 -m http.server 9101` in `~/openvela/nuttx`,
  Windows `Invoke-WebRequest http://192.168.160.128:9101/nuttx.bin`. Check the length.

## Next
Step 2 = `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` + an init call. Put it in the repo-tracked
`esp32s3_appinit.c`, **not** upstream `esp32s3_bringup.c`, to avoid new drift. korvo-2 is
the working reference, but its `SPEAKER_ENABLE_GPIO` write must become a **TCA9554 EXIO7**
expander write on this board ([[velapaw-hardware]]). Then Phase 1.5, TFLM's pre-trained
`micro_speech` ([[velapaw-tflm-onboard]]).

Links: [[velapaw-plan]], [[velapaw-golden-baseline]], [[velapaw-hardware]],
[[openvela-esp32s3-vm-build]].

`py -m serial.tools.miniterm COM4 115200` (Windows, own terminal; quit Ctrl-]) gives a
working `nsh>` immediately. Driving COM4 from a `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort` script gets
**character echo but never a prompt or command output**, on CR/LF/CRLF alike — NuttX
echoes in the driver receive path with or without a reader, so echo is not evidence the
shell is listening. Don't repeat that diagnosis; just use miniterm.

## BLOCKER: no working NSH console

prompt and no command output** — on CR, LF and CRLF alike, and **identically on the

Verified over the console: **`/dev/audio/` contains `pcm0` (TX) and `pcm_in0` (RX)** —
both directions registered. `pcm_in0` is what the wake-word path will read.

## Console: miniterm works, scripts don't

**`py -m serial.tools.miniterm COM4 115200`** from a Windows terminal (quit Ctrl-]) gives
`nsh>` immediately. Driving COM4 from a `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort` script gets
**character echo but never a prompt or any command output**, on CR/LF/CRLF alike.

**Why:** NuttX echoes in the driver receive path with or without a reader, so echo is not
evidence the shell is listening — I briefly mis-read it as a bringup hang. **How to
apply:** for anything needing NSH, have the user run miniterm; don't script the port and
don't re-diagnose this.

text:
Here's the shape of step 2, and one decision I've made:

**Where the codec init goes.** Upstream already has the exact pattern — `board_i2sdev_initialize()` sits in the `#else` of `#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_CS4344`. So ES8311 gets the same treatment: an `#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` branch that calls `esp32s3_es8311_initialize()` instead of the generic path. That's one file changed rather than two, it's where korvo-2 does it, and it makes the collision structurally impossible instead of relying on ordering luck.

**And it becomes a tracked file.** `esp32s3_bringup.c` joins the three files in the README's `cp` list, so this patch is version-controlled rather than a third VM-only edit for `repo sync` to eat.

I need the **VM's** copy of that file to patch, not Windows' — the two `nuttx` trees are at different revisions, and that's exactly what burned us on the `mutex.h` include. In the VM:

```bash
cd ~/openvela/nuttx && python3 -m http.server 9101
```

Tell me when it's up and I'll pull `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit/src/esp32s3_bringup.c`, diff it against the Windows copy so we know what actually differs, then apply the guard.

Also worth flagging now, so it isn't a surprise on the board: enabling `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` is a Kconfig change, so it **will** re-clone esp-hal and revert the spinlock patch. Run `~/fix_hal.sh` before that build — this is the first time it actually earns its keep.

#include "esp32s3-devkit.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * VelaPaw (contest2026_043_CircuitForge) -- ES8311 onboard codec
 *
 * The Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C carries an ES8311 codec on a private
 * I2S bus (IO12 MCLK / IO13 BCLK / IO14 DIN / IO15 WS / IO16 DOUT -- none of
 * which reach a header) with its control interface on I2C0 alongside the touch
 * controller, RTC and IO expander.
 *
 * The devkit board this config is derived from has no ES8311 branch, so we add
 * one mirroring boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-korvo-2/src/esp32s3_bringup.c.
 * The glue itself (esp32s3_es8311_initialize) is NOT korvo-2 private -- it
 * lives in common/src/esp32s3_es8311.c and is compiled whenever
 * CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311=y, so nothing else needs porting.
 *
 * This MUST replace the generic board_i2sdev_initialize() call rather than
 * sit alongside it: both register "pcm0" and "pcm_in0", so whichever runs
 * second fails with -EEXIST.  Note the i2s_enable_tx/rx declaration guard
 * above also excludes ES8311, exactly as korvo-2 does.
 *
 * PA_CTRL (the NS4150B speaker-amp enable) is NOT a GPIO on this board -- it
 * is EXIO7 on the TCA9554 expander, driven from esp32s3_st7789.c.  It is only
 * needed for playback, so it stays off here; the microphone path needs nothing.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311
#  define ES8311_I2C_ADDR  0x18
#  define ES8311_I2C_FREQ  100000

int esp32s3_es8311_initialize(int i2c_port, uint8_t i2c_addr, int i2c_freq,
                              int i2s_port);
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

Step 2 is written. Windows is now serving the repo's `board/` on port 9100.

In the VM — **Ctrl-C the 9101 server first** to free the shell, then:

```bash
BOARD=~/openvela/nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit
wget -q http://192.168.160.1:9100/esp32s3_bringup.c -O $BOARD/src/esp32s3_bringup.c
wget -q http://192.168.160.1:9100/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig -O $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig
grep -n 'ES8311\|AUDIO_ES8311' $BOARD/src/esp32s3_bringup.c $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig | head
cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8 || { ~/fix_hal.sh; ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8; }
```

Only those two files transfer — `esp32s3_st7789.c` and `esp32s3_appinit.c` are unchanged and must not be overwritten (the repo's `st7789.c` differs from the VM's by comments only, and copying it over would be a pointless rebuild). The `||` wrapper handles the esp-hal re-clone that `CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311` will trigger.

What the patch does, in short:

- Adds an `#elif defined(CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311)` branch calling `esp32s3_es8311_initialize(ESP32S3_I2C0, 0x18, 100000, ESP32S3_I2S0)` — mirroring korvo-2, using the shared glue in `common/src/esp32s3_es8311.c`.
- **Replaces** the generic `board_i2sdev_initialize()` rather than adding to it, since both register `pcm0`/`pcm_in0` and the loser gets `-EEXIST`.
- Extends the `i2s_enable_tx/rx` declaration guard, the easy-to-miss half.
- Leaves `PA_CTRL`/EXIO7 alone — playback only, and step 2 is a mic step.

Two things to watch in the build and boot:

`ES8311_NUM_BUFFERS` defaults to 4 at `ES8311_BUFFER_SIZE` 8192 — **32 KB of audio buffers** plus a 2 KB worker stack, on a board with `CONFIG_RAM_SIZE=114688`. If allocation fails at open time, those are the knobs to turn down.

And this is the step the plan flags as able to **hang on I²C**: the codec probe shares I2C0 with the touch controller, RTC and expander. If the board comes up gray with no console, that's the abort signal — reflash the golden binary.

#!/bin/bash
# Every VM-only source patch that `repo sync` or an esp-hal re-clone reverts.
# Idempotent -- safe to run before every build. Supersedes fix_hal.sh.
N=~/openvela/nuttx

add_include () {   # $1=file  $2=header to add  $3=existing anchor include
  [ -f "$1" ] || { echo "skip (absent): $1"; return; }
  grep -q "#include <$2>" "$1" && { echo "ok already:  $1"; return; }
  sed -i "0,\|#include <$3>|s||#include <$3>\n#include <$2>|" "$1"
  echo "patched:     $1"
}

# 1+2. nxmutex_* are static inline in nuttx/mutex.h (LIBC_SEM_MUTEX_NOINLINE=n),
#      so a missing include silently becomes an unresolvable extern at link.

add_include $N/drivers/audio/es8311.c                nuttx/mutex.h nuttx/audio/es8311.h

# 3. esp-hal spinlock: spinlock_t is a struct here, SP_UNLOCKED is a brace
#    initializer, scalar 0 is invalid. Patch EVERY match -- clk_ctrl_os.c is
#    not the first hit, which is why the old head -1 version missed it.
grep -rl 'LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED' $N/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp-hal-3rdparty 2>/dev/null \
| while read -r f; do
  sed -i 's/^\(#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED[[:space:]]*\)0[[:space:]]*$/\1SP_UNLOCKED/' "$f"
done
echo "--- esp-hal spinlock defines ---"
grep -rn '^#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED' $N/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp-hal-3rdparty
EOF
chmod +x ~/fix_vm_patches.sh && ~/fix_vm_patches.sh

/****************************************************************************
 * VelaPaw (contest2026_043_CircuitForge) -- ES8311 onboard codec
 *
 * The Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C carries an ES8311 codec on a private
 * I2S bus (IO12 MCLK / IO13 BCLK / IO14 DIN / IO15 WS / IO16 DOUT -- none of
 * which reach a header) with its control interface on I2C0 alongside the touch
 * controller, RTC and IO expander.
 *
 * The devkit board this config is derived from has no ES8311 branch, so we add
 * one mirroring boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-korvo-2/src/esp32s3_bringup.c.
 * The glue itself (esp32s3_es8311_initialize) is NOT korvo-2 private -- it
 * lives in common/src/esp32s3_es8311.c and is compiled whenever
 * CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311=y, so nothing else needs porting.
 *
 * This MUST replace the generic board_i2sdev_initialize() call rather than
 * sit alongside it: both register "pcm0" and "pcm_in0", so whichever runs
 * second fails with -EEXIST.  Note the i2s_enable_tx/rx declaration guard
 * above also excludes ES8311, exactly as korvo-2 does.
 *
 * PA_CTRL (the NS4150B speaker-amp enable) is NOT a GPIO on this board -- it
 * is EXIO7 on the TCA9554 expander, driven from esp32s3_st7789.c.  It is only
 * needed for playback, so it stays off here; the microphone path needs nothing.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311
#  include <stdint.h>

#  define ES8311_I2C_ADDR  0x18
#  define ES8311_I2C_FREQ  100000

int esp32s3_es8311_initialize(int i2c_port, uint8_t i2c_addr, int i2c_freq,
                              int i2s_port);
#endif
```

274	## PHASE 2 — Dataset
275	
276	`nxrecorder` writes to a filesystem. **There is no microSD** — the slot's pins are the
277	stepper (IO9/10/11). Stream PCM over the USB-CDC console and capture on the host, or
278	buffer to RAM and dump.

280	Record through **this mic, in the printed enclosure, in the real room**, with the
281	stepper running for part of it. A model trained on clean laptop audio will
282	underperform here — mic response, housing resonance, and motor noise all matter.
283	
284	Vocabulary — keep it small, this is a dialog tree, not a sentence parser:
285	
286	```
287	"Hi VelaPaw"  →  "schedule"  →  <pet name>  →  <meal>  →  <hour>
288	```
289	
290	Target ~10–15 words plus silence/unknown.

292	## PHASE 3 — Train (host side)
293	
294	`host/` already has TensorFlow and a working export pipeline from the pet and BCS
295	models. Add a KWS training script alongside them. Target: DS-CNN-S class, int8
296	quantised, **20–40 KB**.

299	it is a known-good model on this exact hardware, so retraining it on your vocabulary
300	keeps the input shape, the preprocessor, and the arena size all unchanged. The only
301	variable becomes the data, which is where the real risk lives.
302	
303	## PHASE 4 — On device
304	
305	Third TFLM interpreter. The pattern is already proven in `app/velapaw/infer/backend_tflm.cc`,
306	which runs two independent interpreters with separate arenas and resolvers — do it a
307	third time with its own `MicroMutableOpResolver<8>` and a ~30 KB arena.
308	
309	**Embed the model in rodata**, do not flash-load it. At this size it rides inside
310	`nuttx.bin` as a `const uint8_t[]` — no flash offset, no `esptool` line, no
311	cache-suspend `.bss`-stack thread. Simplest of the three models by far.

313	### The two real risks (neither is model count)
314	
315	1. **Continuous duty cycle on a single core.** `CONFIG_SMP` is off. Ungated KWS at a
316	   100 ms stride costs ~40 % of the core, permanently, against LVGL + camera + a
317	   1310 ms recognition. **Gate it behind VAD** — `apps/audioutils/speexdsp` is already
318	   in the tree. Cheap DSP decides "is anyone talking"; the expensive model only runs
319	   when the answer is yes. Quiet kitchen → model runs ~never.
320	
321	2. **Audio underrun during the 1310 ms inference.** DMA keeps filling; if the drain
322	   thread isn't scheduled, samples vanish silently and the wake word is missed at
323	   exactly the moment a pet is at the bowl. Two mitigations, both must be designed in:
324	   - audio drain thread priority **above** the recognition worker
325	   - DMA buffers sized for ≥2 s (16 kHz × 16-bit mono = 32 KB/s → 64 KB PSRAM)

327	Do not enable `CONFIG_SMP` to solve this. Recall what `CONFIG_RTC` did to the console.
328

330	
331	Recognized word → the existing schedule path (`velapaw_main.c`, `def_meals[]`) and the
332	Model-B recognition-gated meal times. Screen shows "🎤 Listening…" and echoes the
333	recognized word — the 3.5" display is the audio feedback channel, which is arguably
334	better than a beep and works even if the speaker path lags.
335

337	
338	## Scope honesty
339	
340	Free-form speech — *"velapaw schedule the first feeding time for pet king at 8"* as one
341	spoken sentence — **will not work on-device.** No ASR engine exists in the openVela
342	tree and there is no room for one. On-device gets you a guided dialog tree. The literal
343	sentence requires cloud NLU via `external/bailian_sdk` (`libqwen_sdk.a`,
344	`libc_mmi_cmd_voice_translate.a` are vendored in-tree).
345	
346	Confidence: Phase 1 passing is likely. A *usable* keyword model inside the remaining
347	schedule is roughly a coin flip — the bet is the dataset and training, not the CPU.

## Step 2 ✅ DONE + FLASHED (2026-08-02) — the ES8311 codec itself

`CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311=y` + an init call. `nuttx.bin` **884,844 B** (+67,144 over step 1 —
a real jump, `es8311.o` is referenced so `--gc-sections` can't drop it).

The devkit bringup has no ES8311 branch, so one was added in a **new repo-tracked board
file `board/esp32s3_bringup.c`** (4th `cp` line in README/SESSION_STATE), mirroring
`esp32s3-korvo-2`:
```c
#elif defined(CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311)
  ret = esp32s3_es8311_initialize(ESP32S3_I2C0, 0x18, 100000, ESP32S3_I2S0);
```
🔴 **`#elif`, never an added call.** `board_i2sdev_initialize()` and
`esp32s3_es8311_initialize()` both register `pcm0` *and* `pcm_in0` — whichever runs
second gets `-EEXIST`. Upstream gates the generic path only on `CONFIG_AUDIO_CS4344`, so
ES8311 had to join that guard **and** the `i2s_enable_tx`/`i2s_enable_rx` *declaration*
guard higher up (the easy half to miss; korvo-2 does it at its line 147).
`esp32s3_es8311_initialize()` is in `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/src/`, **not** korvo-2
private, so the devkit needs nothing ported.

On hardware: `[velapaw] ES8311 codec ready on I2C0@0x18 / I2S0`, `/dev/audio/` still
`pcm0`+`pcm_in0`, console/UI/touch/RTC/OV5640/stepper all unaffected. **The codec claims
I2C0 *before* `[wslcd] init`'s expander+touch probes and they still come up clean** —
that shared-bus hang was the whole risk of this step.

**The node names are the proof of success.** With the `#elif` taken,
`board_i2sdev_initialize()` is compiled out — nothing else can register those nodes, so
`pcm0`/`pcm_in0` existing *is* confirmation the codec init returned OK.

`loopback` prints nothing on success — `case OK: break`. So if your prompt came back with no message, it *started* and is running; that's the plan's "silence, no errors" row, not a failure to launch. If instead it printed `No suitable Audio Device found` or the prompt never returned, that's a different problem — tell me which.

Device search is compiled in by default (`NXLOOPER_INCLUDE_DEVICE_SEARCH=y`), so it finds `pcm0`/`pcm_in0` on its own. But with no args it passes **channels=0, bpsamp=0, samprate=0**. Try being explicit:

```
stop
volume 100
loopback 1 16 16000
```

If that's still silent, we've hit the thing `AUDIO_PLAN.md` warned about: none of these failure modes report an error, and I'm not going to guess between mic gain, DAC-only mode, and format mismatch across rebuild cycles. The fix is to make the driver talk — a rebuild with:

```
CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO=y
CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO_ERROR=y
CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO_INFO=y
```

That turns the `auderr()`/`audinfo()` calls all through `es8311.c` and `nxlooper.c` into console output — you'd see the reserve/caps/configure sequence and exactly which ioctl the codec rejects. It's a config-only change, so it costs a re-clone of esp-hal (run `fix_vm_patches.sh`) and one build.

Found it. In `es8311_configure()`, both the INPUT and OUTPUT branches do this:

```c
ret = -ERANGE;                                    /* set up front */
...                                               /* channel + bit-width checks */
ret = es8311_setsamplerate(priv) == -ENOTTY ? OK : ret;
if (ret != OK) break;
```

`ret` is pre-loaded with `-ERANGE` and only ever cleared when `es8311_setsamplerate()` returns **`-ENOTTY`** — i.e. when the I²S layer doesn't implement sample-rate control at all. On a board with a real I²S driver it returns 0 for success, `0 == -ENOTTY` is false, so `ret` stays `-ERANGE` and configure fails **precisely because it worked**. Same pattern at [es8311.c:1045](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.c#L1045) and [es8311.c:1092](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.c#L1092).

That's consistent with everything we've seen: the codec initialises fine, the nodes register, and the very first `AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE` returns 34.

But there's a second path to the same `-ERANGE`, and it matters which one we're on: `es8311_setsamplerate()` also returns `-EINVAL` if `es8311_getcoeff()` can't find the (MCLK, sample-rate) pair in its coefficient table — and that `-EINVAL` gets masked into `-ERANGE` by the same ternary. That would be a real configuration problem, not a code bug, and it'd need an MCLK fix rather than a driver patch.

Confirmed. The table **does** contain `{4096000, 16000}` at [es8311.h:543](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.h#L543) — ten MCLK options for 16 kHz, including ours. So at 16 kHz `getcoeff()` succeeds, `es8311_setsamplerate()` returns 0, and then:

```c
ret = es8311_setsamplerate(priv) == -ENOTTY ? OK : ret;   /* 0 != -ENOTTY → ret stays -ERANGE */
if (ret != OK) break;
```

`configure()` fails *because the hardware setup succeeded*. That's the ternary bug, and it's why the boot-time 48 kHz miss was a red herring — it's a genuinely unsupported pair, but yours isn't.

Fix is mechanical: separate the call from the `-ENOTTY` test. Adding it as VM patch #4:

```bash
cat >> ~/fix_vm_patches.sh <<'EOF'

# 4) es8311.c configure(): ret is pre-loaded with -ERANGE and only cleared when
#    the I2S layer returns -ENOTTY, so a SUCCESSFUL setsamplerate/setbitspersample
#    leaves the error in place and AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE fails with 34.  Upstream bug.
sed -i 's/ret = \(es8311_set[a-z]*\)(priv) == -ENOTTY ? OK : ret;/ret = \1(priv); if (ret == -ENOTTY) ret = OK;/' \
  $N/drivers/audio/es8311.c
echo "--- es8311 configure() ret handling ---"
grep -n 'es8311_setsamplerate(priv)\|es8311_setbitspersample(priv)' $N/drivers/audio/es8311.c
EOF

bash ~/fix_vm_patches.sh
```

Expect four rewritten lines, each now `ret = es8311_setX(priv); if (ret == -ENOTTY) ret = OK;`. The sed is idempotent — it can't match again once applied.

text: `audio_mode` is a single field, and `configure()` **overwrites** it — `es8311_audio_input()` sets `ES_MODULE_ADC`, `es8311_audio_output()` sets `ES_MODULE_DAC`. There's no path that ever sets `ES_MODULE_ADC_DAC`. nxlooper configures record then play, so the second call wins. Whether that's fatal depends on whether both nodes share one device instance:

Good news, and it corrects the concern: `esp32s3_es8311_initialize()` calls `es8311_initialize()` **twice**, creating two independent instances — `g_es8311_lower[0]` → `pcm0` (DAC) and `g_es8311_lower[1]` → `pcm_in0` (ADC). So `audio_mode` is per-node and the two don't clobber each other.

What they *do* share is the physical codec. Both instances call `es8311_reset()` inside `configure()`, reprogramming the same chip registers, and nxlooper configures record first, then play — so the DAC-oriented reset runs last and may leave the ADC path disabled.

text:
Found it — and the fix is one defconfig line, no source patch.

**The chain:**

1. `nxlooper` asks `AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO` → es8311 replies `Unhandled ioctl: 4106` (`-ENOTTY`).
2. In [audio.c:1267-1277](D:/openVela/nuttx/audio/audio.c#L1267-L1277), `upper->nbuffers` is assigned **only when the lower half answers GETBUFFERINFO successfully**. It stayed 0 from the zalloc.
3. [audio.c:786](D:/openVela/nuttx/audio/audio.c#L786): `if (upper->periods >= upper->nbuffers) return 0;` — `0 >= 0` → returns 0.
4. nxlooper checks `ret != sizeof(buf_desc)` → `ERROR: Could not allocate buffer 0`.

It was never a memory shortage — the allocator refused before trying.

And es8311 **already implements** GETBUFFERINFO, at [es8311.c:1806-1813](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.c#L1806-L1813) — the whole case is wrapped in `#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS`, which we never set. Upstream Kconfig bug: `AUDIO_ES8388` carries `select AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS` ([Kconfig:233](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/Kconfig#L233)); `AUDIO_ES8311` ([Kconfig:172](D:/openVela/nuttx/drivers/audio/Kconfig#L172)) doesn't, even though `ES8311_BUFFER_SIZE`/`ES8311_NUM_BUFFERS` are defined unconditionally.

Two things to watch in the next `dmesg`:
- `es8311_ioctl: AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:` **instead of** `Unhandled ioctl: 4106` — that's the fix landing.
- `es8311_start` on both nodes, followed by `es8311_enqueuebuffer` traffic. If those appear and it's still silent, *then* the amp/mic is finally the suspect — up to now nothing had ever reached the codec.

## Step 3 IN PROGRESS — PA_CTRL + the `nxlooper` ear test

**`PA_CTRL` is done.** The NS4150B enable is **TCA9554 EXIO7, not a GPIO**, so the ES8311
driver cannot reach it. `board_speaker_enable(bool)` was added to `esp32s3_st7789.c`
(next to the existing `g_ioe` handle) and is asserted at boot under
`#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_ES8311`. Confirmed on hardware:
`[velapaw] speaker amp enabled (PA_CTRL = EXIO7)`. It is exported rather than inlined so
the app can gate the amp per-playback later — leaving it on idles the amp and can hiss.

**🔴 `nxlooper` cannot allocate buffers unless `CONFIG_AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS=y`.**
Symptom: `loopback` returns to the prompt with no error, nothing is audible, and `dmesg`
shows `nxlooper_loopthread: ERROR: Could not allocate buffer 0` — the loop thread tears
down immediately, so **nothing ever reaches the codec** and neither the amp nor the mic
is implicated. The chain:

1. nxlooper issues `AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO`; es8311 answers `Unhandled ioctl: 4106`.
2. `audio.c:1267` sets `upper->nbuffers` **only** when the lower half answers that ioctl
   successfully, so it stays 0 from the zalloc.
3. `audio_allocbuffer()` (`audio.c:786`) opens with
   `if (upper->periods >= upper->nbuffers) return 0;` → `0 >= 0` → returns 0.
4. nxlooper requires `ret == sizeof(buf_desc)`, sees 0, and errors out.

It is **not** memory pressure — the allocator refuses before it ever tries. es8311
already implements the handler at `es8311.c:1806`; the whole `case` is wrapped in
`#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS`. Upstream Kconfig miss: `AUDIO_ES8388`
carries `select AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS`, `AUDIO_ES8311` does not, even though
`ES8311_BUFFER_SIZE`/`ES8311_NUM_BUFFERS` are defined unconditionally. **Fix is one
defconfig line, no source patch.** Gives 4 × 8 KB per direction = 64 KB, and at 16 kHz
mono ≈256 ms per buffer, so the ear test will echo about a second late. That is expected.

**Debug-only defconfig entries to back out before shipping:** `CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO`,
`CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO_ERROR`, `CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO_INFO`, `CONFIG_DEBUG_AUDIO_WARN`,
`CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES`, `CONFIG_RAMLOG_BUFSIZE=16384`.

### Reading the RAMLOG

**`dmesg` does not drain the buffer, and a full buffer drops new messages.** The 1024 B
default filled during boot with `DEBUG_AUDIO_INFO` on, so every post-boot message was
discarded and three consecutive `dmesg` runs returned byte-identical boot text — which
reads exactly like "nothing is happening" when in fact nothing was being *recorded*.
`CONFIG_RAMLOG_BUFSIZE=16384` fixes it; RAMLOG lives in `.bss` so `nuttx.bin` is unchanged.

NSH has **no pipe** and its `dmesg` takes **no arguments** — `dmesg | grep es8311` gives
"too many arguments". `dmesg` is also not an `nxlooper` command; type it at `nsh>` only.
Prefer `q` over `stop` to end a loopback: `quit` stops the loop itself, so it is one
blocking call rather than two.

### Console: use miniterm, not a script

"""Drive the NuttX CDCACM console on COM4.

The earlier PowerShell System.IO.Ports attempt got echo but never a prompt:
SerialPort leaves DtrEnable false, and CDCACM only reports the host as
connected once DTR is asserted -- which miniterm does by default.
"""

import sys
import time

import serial

PORT = "COM4"
BAUD = 115200


def drain(ser, seconds, out):
    """Read everything that arrives for `seconds`, echoing as we go."""
    end = time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end:
        n = ser.in_waiting
        if n:
            chunk = ser.read(n)
            out.write(chunk)
            end = time.time() + seconds  # keep reading while it is still talking
        else:
            time.sleep(0.05)


def send(ser, line, wait, out):
    out.write(b"\n===> " + line.encode() + b"\n")
    ser.write(line.encode() + b"\r")
    ser.flush()
    drain(ser, wait, out)


def main():
    ser = serial.Serial()
    ser.port = PORT
    ser.baudrate = BAUD
    ser.timeout = 0.2
    ser.dtr = True          # the bit PowerShell got wrong
    ser.rts = True
    ser.open()

    out = open(sys.argv[1], "wb")
    try:
        ser.reset_input_buffer()
        send(ser, "", 1.0, out)              # bare CR -- do we get a prompt?
        send(ser, "nxlooper", 1.5, out)
        send(ser, "loopback 1 16 16000", 3.0, out)
        send(ser, "q", 1.5, out)
        send(ser, "dmesg", 10.0, out)
    finally:
        out.close()
        ser.close()


main()

What this changes: syslog goes **live to COM4** instead of into a buffer you can only read with `dmesg`. So when it hangs, whatever the kernel prints on the way down — an assertion, a hardfault dump, a stack trace — lands on your screen as it happens. Dropping `DEBUG_AUDIO_INFO` keeps the boot from drowning in ES8311 register dumps while leaving `auderr`/`audwarn` intact.

I've been chasing this through `dmesg` the whole time, which only works if the board survives to give you a prompt. It hasn't been surviving. This makes the failure visible at the moment it happens instead.

Those two `-22` lines are the benign ones: that's `es8311_reset()` calling `setsamplerate` at the driver's own 48 kHz default before our 16 kHz gets applied, and the reset path deliberately ignores the return. `q` hanging is the last piece. `nxlooper_stop()` joins the loop thread, and that thread is parked in `mq_receive` waiting for a buffer that never completes — so the record side never returns a single buffer. Combined with no sound, that's a coherent picture, and I think I can name the mechanism. Look at the order in [nxlooper.c:477-489](D:/openVela/apps/system/nxlooper/nxlooper.c#L477-L489) and [nxlooper.c:576-583](D:/openVela/apps/system/nxlooper/nxlooper.c#L576-L583): it starts **record** first, and only starts **play** after the first record buffer comes back. If RX depends on a clock that TX generates, that's a deadlock by construction.
